verses.text: For the music director. A psalm by David. A song. Let God rise up! Let his enemies scatter and those who hate him run from him!
Drive them away like smoke in the wind. Let the wicked perish before God like wax melting in the fire.
Let the righteous be glad. Let them rejoice before God and celebrate with joy.
Sing to God! Sing praise to his name! Honor the one who rides on the clouds. His name is the LORD. Rejoice before him!
God in his holy dwelling is a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows.
God gives lonely people a family and leads prisoners out singing, while those who rebel live in a land scorched by the sun.
God, when you went out ahead of your people and marched through the wilderness… Selah.
The earth shook and the sky poured down rain before the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
You sent abundant rain, God. You restored your inheritance when it was worn out.
Your people settled there. In your goodness, God, you provided for the poor.
The Lord gave the word, and a great crowd spread the news.
“Kings and their armies are running! They’re running!” The women at home divide what was taken,
while you rest among the campfires, the wings of a dove covered in silver and its feathers shining with gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
The mountains of Bashan are majestic. The mountains of Bashan rise in rugged peaks.
Why do you rugged mountains look with envy at the mountain God chose to rule from? The LORD will live there forever.
God’s chariots number in the tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands. The Lord is among them, coming from Sinai into the sanctuary.
You went up on high and led captives away. You received gifts from people, even from those who rebelled, so that the LORD God might live there.
Blessed be the Lord! Day after day he carries our burdens, the God who saves us. Selah.
Our God is a God who rescues. The Lord GOD has the power to save from death.
God will strike the heads of his enemies, the hairy scalps of those who keep walking in their guilt.
The Lord said, “I’ll bring them back from Bashan. I’ll bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so you can crush them and dip your feet in blood, and your dogs can have their share of your enemies.”
People have seen your procession, God, the procession of my God and King into the sanctuary.
The singers went first. The musicians followed, among young women playing tambourines.
“Bless God in the gatherings. Bless the Lord in the assembly of Israel!”
There’s little Benjamin leading them, the leaders of Judah with their crowd, and the leaders of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Your God has commanded your strength. Show your strength, God, and uphold what you’ve done for us.
Because of your temple in Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
Rebuke the beast among the reeds and the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample their bars of silver. Scatter the nations that love war.
Princes will come from Egypt. Ethiopia will hurry to stretch out its hands to God.
Sing to God, kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord. Selah.
Sing to the one who rides through the ancient highest heavens. Listen as he raises his mighty voice.
Give God the credit for his strength! His majesty is over Israel, and his power fills the skies.
God, you fill us with awe in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives his people strength and power. Praise be to God!
